title: Chromate-Free Protection and Drainage Path Standard at the Fwd Cargo Door Surround

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: Introduction of a chromate-free protective scheme and a defined water escape route at the forward cargo door surround, replacing the original sealing arrangement that trapped moisture behind the frame feet of the lower shell.

sections.reason: In-service inspection of aircraft above 40 000 flight hours found filiform and pitting corrosion behind the frame feet of the forward cargo door surround on twenty-three aircraft out of a sampled population of ninety-four. The original build sealed the frame foot to the skin along its full length, so condensate running down the frame web collected at the foot and had no route to the drain path. The chromated primer used at build is also being withdrawn under the applicable environmental regulation, which forced a protective scheme change on the same timescale. The two drivers were combined into a single change rather than run as two sequential modifications.
sections.description: The frame feet of the door surround structure are re-worked so that the faying surface is sealed only at its forward and aft ends, leaving a 12 mm interrupted land at the lowest point of each foot through which water can reach the stringer 46 drain path. The door surround fitting kit D5321131361369 and the inboard surround frame sub-assembly D5321134517524 are re-issued with the revised sealing land machined in. Fastener holes are wet-installed with a chromate-free polysulphide and the joint is re-fastened with washers AES963502K7 and EN736536-59 in place of the previous cadmium-plated set; plain washers AGS46790-6A are used at the shear ties. All new surfaces receive the chromate-free primer of the standard practice for surface treatment. Revised detail is on drawing D53211323435. Access is through the forward cargo compartment in zones 111 and 121 with the lower shell lining removed, and through the door aperture itself in zone 891.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 0.8 kg per aircraft, symmetric, with no reportable balance effect. No electrical load change. The re-worked frame feet are one-way interchangeable: a post-modification foot may be installed on a pre-modification aircraft but not the reverse, because the pre-modification sealing land does not clear the new drain interruption. The zonal corrosion inspection of the forward cargo compartment lower shell moves from a 4C interval to a 6C interval once embodied. AMM zonal and cleaning content for ATA 53-21 and the corrosion prevention and control programme require update, and the IPC surround figure needs a pre and post effectivity split.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN S00992 in May 2019. Retrofit for delivered aircraft is through Service Bulletin SLN-53-1012, which is preceded by the borescope and eddy current survey of SLN-53-1008 so that the extent of existing corrosion is known before the frame feet are disturbed. Typical embodiment is five days inside a scheduled C-check.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN S00992, absorbed in the Section 13 build sequence at Port-Rivage

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: Introduction of a chromate-free protective scheme and a defined water escape route at the forward cargo door surround, replacing the sealing arrangement that trapped moisture behind the frame feet, and now the declared baseline for any later floor penetration in the same drain path.

sections.reason: In-service inspection of aircraft above 40 000 flight hours found filiform and pitting corrosion behind the frame feet of the forward cargo door surround on twenty-three aircraft out of a sampled population of ninety-four. sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN S00992 in May 2019. Typical embodiment is five days inside a scheduled C-check. An operator planning a later freighter conversion should embody this change first, because the hard point provisioning cannot be released onto an aircraft at the original sealing standard.
